theme_and_runs.why: Unmistakably a mini-game with goal, live feedback and distinct win/tie-loss/loss states; I drove a full five-level playthrough to the ending screen with a completely clean console, all 25 automated checks pass, refused clicks (non-adjacent, already-assigned, board-full) are visibly rejected with clear live-region messages and never corrupt counts, and with localStorage throwing SecurityError the game stayed fully playable and told the player so.

originality.why: Grid-partition gerrymandering — equal-size contiguous districts where the minority colour wins the council on seats — is nowhere near the banned clone list and is a genuinely uncommon mechanic, but gerrymandering explainer/puzzle demos are recognisable prior art, so it is a fresh execution of an idea some jurors will have met rather than a new one.

ux_design.why: Coherent dark palette, dot-vs-ring shape redundancy, thick region outlines with corner rounding that genuinely read as districts, live tallies on board and chips, ARIA live region, dialog focus trap, and an exact 44px cell on the 7x7 board at 375x667 with no page scroll at 320/375/1440 — but the desktop view is a 640px phone-shaped column with a left-aligned title stranded in a mostly empty 1440px viewport, and entering Play leaves keyboard focus off the grid.

prompt_quality.why: Dense behavioural spec that anticipates the real unsupervised-agent traps (file:// modules, storage that throws, stuck drag state, listeners in a loop) and, best of all, orders the agent to write and run a throwaway brute force proving every level winnable then delete it — which demonstrably worked; docked because section 8's checklist restates sections 5-7 near-verbatim.

reproducibility.why: Screens, controls, rules, constraints and the difficulty arc are all pinned tightly enough that a rerun reproduces the same game; the boards are deliberately left to the agent, and the winnability guarantee leans on the agent actually running a solver — the prompt's 'or trace it by hand' fallback is the one path that could ship an unwinnable finale.

key_features_a_rerun_must_reproduce: Five hand-designed levels, each verified winnable, where the player carves the grid into exactly-equal orthogonally contiguous districts and Teal takes more seats than Amber despite losing the popular vote

Draw-by-adjacency input (pointer drag, click and arrow-key cursor) that makes contiguity impossible to break, with visible refusal of illegal cells, undo/clear, and a per-district running tally on the board
A result screen that puts popular vote and seat count side by side so the trick is visible, plus a plain-language 'here's why' screen when the board fills without Teal winning
Single offline index.html that survives localStorage throwing, respects prefers-reduced-motion, and fits a 375x667 phone with no scrolling and 44px tap targets
biggest_weakness: The desktop presentation is the weak link: the whole game is a 640px mobile-shaped column adrift in a 1440px viewport, with the title screen's left-aligned block reading as a mis-centred accident rather than a choice, and no wide layout for the play screen even though the board, status bar, chips and controls would sit naturally side by side.
single_highest_leverage_fix: Add a >=900px layout that puts the board beside the status/chips/controls column (and centres or deliberately anchors the title block), and focus the grid on entering a level so arrow keys work without hunting for Tab.
